newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end sharply higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle closed sharply higher and near best levels of the day in nearby live cattle as firmer cash cattle ideas added to short covering and technical support, traders said.
Live cattle closed 1.000 to 0.175 cent per lb higher with April up most at 68.700 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.975 to 0.400 higher with May up 0.900 at 68.450 cents.

A sharp setback in grain futures early sparked early demand in feeder cattle which spilled over into live cattle futures, sources said. Live cattle then turned technically strong and rallied further on buy stops, traders said.

April live cattle were technically oversold and also held support after recently posting a 50 percent retracement from recent highs. Prices held Monday's lows which added to the technical reversal, sources said.
The strength in live cattle futures prompted feedlots to raise asking prices. Packers in turn, raised bids for cash cattle to price levels near steady with last week.
"The feeling is, we could see cash cattle rebound back up close to this $70 mark again," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities Inc. "Feedlot asking prices went up."
